newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. envoy expects no Cyprus missile deployment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy expects no Cyprus missile deployment.

text.p: U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh on Wednesday predicted that a planned missile deployment in Cyprus that has angered NATO member Turkey would not take place.
"It is my personal expectation those missiles will never come to the island," Cavanaugh told reporters on arrival at Ankara airport from Athens.
Cavanaugh repeated U.S. objections to the planned purchase by Cyprus of S-300 anti-aircraft missiles from Russia. The rockets are due on the island in 16 months.
"This is not something we support. This is not something we favour and this is not something we will favour in 16 months. The solution has to be found," he said.
He said Washington also opposed Turkish threats to halt the deployment by force: "No aggressive response can be justified or accepted."
Ankara threatened several times last week to take military action if the S-300s were sent to Cyprus, where Turkey backs a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north.
Both sides on Cyprus have denied the missile crisis is over, despite comments by Cavanaugh after talks on the island that the row had been defused.
The Cypriot administration, internationally regarded as the island's only government, says it will go ahead with the installation of the system after 16 months if no breakthrough has been made.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a coup in Nicosia backed by the military government then ruling Greece. Turkey keeps some 30,000 troops in the north of the island.
